events.text: A young immortal with a famous master has been cutting down every challenger on an isle for a month, and laughing at them after. Nobody stops it, because nobody wants the master's anger. The Sword Dao in you knows exactly what must be cut here, and it is not the young one's life.

choices.text: Meet the young one sword to sword, and cut only the pride

ok.log: One exchange, and the young one's sword is in the grass and their sleeve is in two pieces. They stop laughing. You feel the realm settle a little deeper into you.

fail.log: The young one is better than the stories said. You hold your own, no more, and walk away with the lesson in your arm.

choices.text: Show them a single cut on a falling leaf, and let them understand

ok.log: You cut a falling leaf so that it lands in two halves that still touch. The young one goes quiet, and bows. The Dao settles in you like a blade into its sheath.

fail.log: The leaf falls whole. The young one smirks. Still, you understood something about cutting, even if they did not.

choices.text: Leave it to their master, and spend the season cutting practice posts alone

effects.log: You cut ten thousand posts that season, each one a little cleaner. It is the Sword Dao lived small, and it still counts.

events.text: Two houses of an isle have tied their quarrel into a knot that nobody can untie: an old marriage, a broken promise, a debt on a debt. They come to you because they have heard that the Sword Dao cuts what must be cut. They expect a ruling. You see a knot.

choices.text: Find the one thread the whole knot hangs on, and cut it

ok.log: It was the old promise, never the debt. You name it, both houses go pale, and the knot comes apart in your hands. The realm feels lighter on your shoulders.

fail.log: You cut the wrong thread. The knot tightens, and both houses leave angrier than they came. You understood the cut too late.

choices.text: Draw your sword between them, and dare either to cross it

ok.log: Nobody crosses it. In the silence they find they would rather talk than bleed, and they talk until dawn. A cut that drew nothing settles you deeper than any duel.

fail.log: One of them crosses it, and you have to put them down without harm. The talk never starts. The realm settles only a little.

choices.text: Tell them plainly what you see, and leave the cutting to them

effects.log: You tell them what you see. They do not like it, and they do not forget it. The Dao settles in you a hair.

events.text: Reavers have been taking skiffs on the far roads of the Isles, and the guards who go after them do not come back. The Blade Dao is not the Sword: it is weight and edge and going through. You take your blade and go out on the road.

choices.text: Go through them, all of them, edge first

ok.log: They had never met anything that did not stop. They scatter like chaff, and the road is quiet behind you. Each blow sinks the realm deeper into your bones.

fail.log: There are more of them than the guards said. You come back with the road half cleared and a new respect for numbers.

choices.text: Find their leader and take the blade from their hand

ok.log: You catch the leader's blade on your own and twist, and it is yours. The rest put theirs down. The Blade Dao settles in you like iron cooling.

fail.log: The leader lets go before you can take it, and flees with the rest. The road will need you again.

choices.text: Ride guard on the skiffs for a season instead

effects.log: You ride guard all season. Nobody attacks a skiff with you on it. Half the deed, and all of the road safe for a while.

events.text: A master smith of an isle has forged a blade she thinks is the best of her life, and asks you to test it, because only one who lives the Blade Dao can tell. She warns you: a blade that is not tested to breaking has not been tested.

fail.log: It breaks on the third blow, and the smith goes white. Still, she thanks you. A true answer is worth a blade.

choices.text: Read its flaw before you swing it

fail.log: You see no flaw, and there was one. It cracks in your hand. Both of you learned something.

choices.text: Praise it and hand it back unswung

effects.log: She takes it back with a look you do not enjoy. Still, you held it, and the Blade Dao in you knew it.

events.text: A sickness has come up from the world below with a skiff of pilgrims, and the cloud-herders of an isle are falling to it one by one. Immortals do not catch such things. Immortals also do not usually come down from their halls to sit with the sick.

choices.text: Sit with them and draw the sickness out, one by one

ok.log: It takes all season. You lose none of them. The Dao of Life settles into you like water into a root.

fail.log: You save most of them. Not all. The ones you lost teach you as much as the ones you saved.

choices.text: Find where it came from and cut it at the root

ok.log: It was the water in the pilgrims' casks. You burn the casks and the sickness ends in a week. The realm settles deeper.

fail.log: You do not find the source in time, and it burns itself out on its own. You learned how it moves, at least.

choices.text: Send your best pills and a healer you trust

effects.log: The pills save most of them, and the healer comes back changed. You did good from a distance, and the Dao counts half of it.

effects.log: You leave with nothing in your hands and much less in your head. That is half the Void's way.

events.text: The great water-clock of an isle, which has kept time for ten thousand years, has stopped. Nobody alive knows how it was built. The Dao of Time hums in you when you look at it.

choices.text: Follow its gears back to the first one, and start it again

choices.text: Let it flower alone

choices.text: Hold the crack shut with your hand on the bronze

ok.log: You hold it shut through the whole turn, and your hand blisters, and the pill turns clean.

fail.log: The crack opens for a breath. The fire falters, and the pill loses a turn.

choices.text: Mend the furnace without stopping the fire

choices.text: Put out the fire and give up the pill

effects.log: You put out the fire. Nine years of turning go into the ash.

events.text: {c1_work} is a third raised, and the land has started to drift: it wants to go where the wind goes, and if it drifts too far it will break apart in the high winds.

choices.text: Anchor it to the Isles with your own qi

ok.log: You anchor it with a cord of your own qi, and it stops drifting, and its roots grow toward the cord.

fail.log: The anchor slips once. It drifts into the high winds for a night and loses years of growth.

choices.text: Read the wind and let it drift where it is safe

fail.log: You read the wind wrong. It drifts into a storm and loses years.

events.text: {c1_work} is two thirds raised, and a house of immortals has noticed it: unclaimed land, they say, is anyone's land. They have come to set their stones on it.

choices.text: Drive them off it

ok.log: They go, and tell everyone that the land has a master.

fail.log: They set their stones on one edge before you drive them off. That edge has to be raised again.

choices.text: Catch them at the flags
